data.title: Choose the sentence that uses the word correctly.

sections.question: climate change
sections.summary: Long-term shifts in global temperatures and weather patterns, largely caused by human activities such as burning fossil fuels.

senses.definition: the long-term shift in global temperatures and weather patterns, primarily caused by human activities such as burning fossil fuels
examples: Scientists warn that climate change is leading to more frequent and severe weather events worldwide.

senses.definition: more broadly, any significant long-term change in the expected patterns of climate in a region
examples: Governments around the world are being urged to take urgent action to slow the effects of climate change.

answers.answer: The documentary explained how climate change is affecting wildlife habitats across the globe.
She experienced a climate change when she moved from the UK to Australia and needed time to adjust.
He needed a climate change from the school library before writing his geography essay.
The teacher asked every student to bring a climate change to the next lesson for the project.

sections.question: conservation
sections.summary: The careful protection of natural environments, wildlife and resources to prevent their destruction or waste.

senses.definition: the protection of natural environments, animals and plants from damage or destruction
examples: Wildlife conservation efforts have helped increase the wild tiger population significantly.

senses.definition: the careful use of resources to avoid unnecessary waste
examples: The government launched a campaign promoting energy conservation in homes and businesses.

answers.answer: Marine conservation programmes have helped protect endangered coral reefs around the world.
She had a long conservation with her professor after the lecture about the upcoming assignment.
He filed the conservation carefully into his folder at the end of the lesson.
The conservation was so interesting that all the students chose to stay behind for fifteen extra minutes.

sections.question: deforestation
sections.summary: The large-scale cutting down and removal of trees from forested areas, often to use the land for farming or development.

senses.definition: the process of cutting down and removing all the trees from a large area of land, often to use the land for farming, industry or development
examples: Rapid deforestation in the Amazon rainforest is destroying critical habitats for thousands of species.

answers.answer: The report highlighted how deforestation is one of the leading causes of biodiversity loss.
She studied deforestation to learn the best techniques for planting new trees in urban areas.
The class visited a deforestation at the weekend to learn about different species of tree.
He brought a deforestation to class to show the teacher as part of his research project.

sections.question: ecosystem
sections.summary: All the plants, animals and other living things in an area, together with the non-living parts of their environment, forming a complex system.

senses.definition: all the living organisms in an area together with the non-living parts of their environment, which interact as a system
examples: The coral reef ecosystem supports an extraordinary variety of fish and marine life.

senses.definition: a complex network of interconnected parts that function together as a whole
examples: The tech industry has developed a thriving digital ecosystem around the new platform.

answers.answer: Draining the wetlands would destroy a fragile ecosystem that took thousands of years to develop.
She bought a new ecosystem from the science supply shop to use in the laboratory experiment.
He left his ecosystem on the bus and had to borrow one from a classmate for the lesson.
The students set up an ecosystem at the front of the class to present their survey findings.

sections.question: endangered species
sections.summary: A type of animal or plant that is at serious risk of becoming extinct because its numbers in the wild have fallen to very low levels.

senses.definition: a type of animal or plant that exists in such small numbers that it is at serious risk of becoming extinct
examples: The mountain gorilla was once considered one of the most critically endangered species on the planet.

answers.answer: New conservation laws have been passed to protect several endangered species from illegal hunting.
She listed her favourite endangered species of music and discussed each one in her essay.
The teacher collected the endangered species from every student at the end of the lesson.
He ordered three endangered species from the internet to use in his school science project.

sections.question: environmental protection
sections.summary: Actions, laws and policies designed to keep the natural environment safe from damage caused by human activity.

senses.definition: the protection of the natural environment through laws, policies and individual actions that reduce human damage
examples: The new legislation focuses on environmental protection by placing strict limits on industrial emissions.

answers.answer: The government agency is responsible for enforcing environmental protection laws across the country.
She applied environmental protection to her hands and face before going out into the midday sun.
He used environmental protection to keep his flat warm and lower his heating bills in winter.
The school introduced environmental protection for any student who arrived late to class three times.

sections.question: pollution
sections.summary: Harmful substances that have been introduced into the natural environment, making air, water or land dirty or unsafe.

senses.definition: damage caused to air, water or land by harmful substances or waste
examples: Air pollution in many major cities has reached dangerously high levels during the summer months.

senses.definition: the substances that cause environmental damage
examples: The river was closed to swimmers after high levels of pollution were detected in the water.

answers.answer: The factory was fined heavily for releasing pollution directly into the local river.
She felt great pollution after cleaning the entire classroom by herself before the inspection.
He used pollution to heat the water in the science experiment more quickly and efficiently.
The students completed a pollution together in class to practise their mathematical equations.

sections.question: recycling
sections.summary: The process of converting used materials or waste into new materials or products so that they can be used again.

senses.definition: the process of treating used or waste materials so that they can be used again
examples: The school introduced a recycling scheme to reduce the amount of plastic waste it sends to landfill.

senses.definition: to treat waste materials so that they can be used again
examples: The company recycles over eighty percent of the materials used in its manufacturing process.

answers.answer: The council expanded its recycling programme to include glass, plastic and food waste.
She put the recycling into the general waste bin so it would not be kept separate from the rubbish.
He stayed late to finish his recycling and handed it to the teacher before leaving class.
The students did recycling together the evening before the important geography examination.

sections.question: renewable energy
sections.summary: Energy produced from natural sources that are constantly replenished and will not run out, such as sunlight, wind, water and geothermal heat.

senses.definition: energy from natural sources that are replenished continuously and will not run out, such as the sun, wind and water
examples: Solar panels and wind turbines are among the most widely used sources of renewable energy.

answers.answer: The country has invested heavily in renewable energy and now produces most of its power from wind farms.
She drank renewable energy before the long examination to help her stay focused and alert.
He bought renewable energy from the local shop to use as a power source in his experiment.
The students showed great renewable energy by volunteering to stay behind and tidy the laboratory.

sections.question: sustainability
sections.summary: The ability to be maintained over the long term without causing permanent damage to the environment or depleting natural resources.

senses.definition: the quality of being able to continue over a long period without harming the environment or using up natural resources
examples: The company made sustainability a central part of its long-term business strategy.

senses.definition: the ability of a process or situation to be maintained at a certain level without causing damage or decline
examples: Economists are questioning the sustainability of the country's rapid economic growth.

answers.answer: The report assessed the sustainability of current fishing levels in the North Atlantic.
She demonstrated great sustainability by completing all her assignments well before every single deadline.
He carried his sustainability to school every day in his backpack throughout the entire project.
The teacher gave each student a sustainability to work through quietly during the afternoon session.
